title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: Sources: Jay Clayton, director of national intelligence and AI czar, will also be acting national cyber director pending Kirsten A. Davies' Senate confirmation (Axios)
items.content_text: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton will serve as acting national cyber director to address escalating cyber threats and infrastructure vulnerabilities while awaiting Senate confirmation of Kirsten A. Davies. This move centralizes oversight to ensure policy cohesion during the transitional period.

items.title: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird
items.content_text: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and President Daniela Amodei defended their $900 billion AI infrastructure commitments ahead of their IPO, emphasizing a balanced approach between rapid growth and responsible AI development. The founders reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining an atypical organizational culture while scaling computing resources.

items.title: U.S. Tracked Alice Huang’s Contacts With China Spy Agency During Nvidia Affair
items.content_text: U.S. intelligence reports reveal that Alice Huang, a central figure in the scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, maintained consistent contact with Chinese Ministry of State Security officers from spring 2025 through autumn 2024. Investigations indicate that she and her business associate, Kang Wei, utilized their company, Megaspeed, to create a supply chain network that diverted advanced Nvidia chips to Southeast Asian data centers and potentially smuggled restricted hardware into China.

items.title: Inside an AI prophet’s secretive visions for humanity’s future
items.content_text: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei recently hosted briefings for academics and think tank fellows to showcase how the company's 'AI constitution' guides model behavior. The firm holds a deterministic view that AI will soon surpass human intelligence, prioritizing moral alignment as a core mechanism to mitigate systemic risks.

items.title: We haven’t seen the last of the major tech outages
items.content_text: US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Microsoft President Brad Smith warned that recent outages in aviation and banking systems underscore systemic infrastructure fragility. They emphasized that AI adoption has lowered the barrier for attackers to identify code vulnerabilities, leading to an increased frequency of cyber threats against government and commercial targets.

items.title: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warns Americans of 'bumps in the road' after tech outages
items.content_text: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that Americans should expect intermittent service outages as government and critical infrastructure undergo systemic upgrades for AI integration. Recent technology disruptions, including those affecting Microsoft Outlook and air travel, have been attributed to network capacity patches rather than AI-related cyberattacks.

items.title: Bessent Calls on Nvidia to Provide Answers on Chip Sales to China
items.content_text: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has demanded a thorough investigation into the supply chain pathways and compliance failures regarding the unauthorized shipment of Nvidia’s advanced chips to China. Following a scandal involving former CEO Jensen Huang and alleged Chinese intelligence assets, Huang is scheduled to testify at a closed-door House hearing on December 1st to address whether the non-compliance was a result of internal malice or systematic failure.

items.title: Binding of Isaac developer removes AI music from Repentance Plus
items.content_text: Edmund McMillen and Nicalis, Inc. integrated AI-generated music containing Suno metadata into 'The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus', violating Valve's mandatory disclosure policy for generative AI and triggering a review-bombing campaign on Steam. Nicalis has since removed the files via a patch, while McMillen issued an apology claiming no prior knowledge of the assets.

items.title: Like SpaceX, Anthropic ran an unusual IPO process, chafing some bankers
items.content_text: Business Recorder • 22 Nov 2026, 5:00 PM PKT • 1 min read Business Recorder reported that Anthropic’s IPO, which took place on Thursday, raised more than half a billion dollars in underwriting fees but drew complaints from some bankers about the way it was run. The offering surpassed SpaceX’s June listing, and bankers cited a compressed timetable, late changes, delayed financial projections and rushed approvals. items.title: AI coding agents ace isolated tests but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace
items.content_text: In a simulated software development environment featuring project boards, chat logs, and collaborative workflows, leading models like GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 achieved a task completion rate of less than 10%. The findings highlight a critical performance gap between high scores on isolated code benchmarks and the requirements of complex, collaborative system engineering.

items.title: The Internet Broke Our Taste. Will A.I. Destroy It for Good?
items.content_text: Silicon Valley is increasingly defining 'taste' as the ultimate human moat against generative AI's algorithmic slop. The current industry debate centers on whether aesthetic judgment is merely a pattern-matching exercise achievable by LLMs, or a uniquely human cognitive capability that determines future market valuation of creative output.

items.title: Perplexity's new Monitor API turns web search from a one-off query into a nonstop watchdog
items.content_text: Perplexity has launched the Monitor API, allowing developers to define monitoring goals via natural language for periodic scanning of specific web pages or global information. The service integrates a decision model to filter out noise, pushing verified updates via webhooks only when findings meet predefined criteria for relevance, credibility, and novelty.

items.title: AI is getting better faster than experts can reliably test whether new systems are safe, METR warns
items.content_text: AI research evaluation firm METR reports that large models are closing the gap with human experts in coding and computational tasks, with the complexity of autonomous tasks they can handle doubling every 3.6 months. METR warns that current evaluation environments consistently overestimate model performance for real-world scenarios, and if this trajectory continues, models are projected to reach a 50% success rate on 200-hour complex tasks by July 2027, potentially exceeding human capacity to monitor catastrophic risks.

items.title: The vibe-coding revolution is coming to all the gadgets
items.content_text: A new wave of hardware customization, termed 'vibe-coding,' is emerging as developers utilize large language models like Claude Code and Codex to simplify low-level hardware configuration. By automating interactions such as modifying Android TV interfaces and bypassing bloatware via USB debugging, this trend is significantly lowering the barrier for end-user control over proprietary hardware, fueling a grassroots movement for open-device ecosystems.

items.title: Security researchers show how cheap AI inference providers steal keys and snoop on users
items.content_text: Security firm Dragos revealed between July and November 2026 that multiple AI inference providers failed to uphold data retention policies, leading to the theft of AWS keys and sensitive user requests. Investigations confirmed that some marketplace resellers enabled logging to intercept data, with instances of leaked test URLs being accessed within minutes from Beijing and Shanghai via internal communication platforms.

items.title: Lean and Mathlib community officially confirms Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct
items.content_text: Stanford mathematician Levent Alpöge published a proof of the Riemann hypothesis on November 20, 2026, consisting of 17 million lines of Lean code. The Lean and Mathlib community confirmed the proof's correctness through independent execution and formal verification, officially resolving the century-old mathematical challenge.

items.title: The AI cyber threat is already here
items.content_text: Cybersecurity experts warn that AI tools significantly accelerate the time required for attackers to parse complex industrial control system (ICS) manuals and analyze historical accident data. This shift lowers the barrier to entry for executing targeted attacks on critical infrastructure and enables exponential speed gains in the reconnaissance phase.

items.title: Banks Have Had It Up to Here With Your AI Agent
items.content_text: Major US financial institutions, including Wells Fargo, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and Citibank, have updated their terms of service to restrict or ban third-party AI agents from accessing user accounts via credentials. These measures aim to mitigate risks of unauthorized transactions, data breaches, and human error induced by automated agents, placing full liability on the users.

items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol get to the point faster but score lower on transparency than Claude
items.content_text: OpenAI's latest GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models have shifted towards high-efficiency interaction in Artificial Analysis benchmarks, reducing average response lengths by 40% and 34% respectively. By deprioritizing structured formatting and uncertainty disclosure, these models achieve faster direct answers, whereas Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 maintain superior performance in transparency and organizational indices.

items.title: China’s Spies Set Sights on A.I. Chips Years Before Nvidia Scandal
items.content_text: China's Ministry of State Security, led by Minister Chen Yixin, has established a specialized task force reporting directly to him to bypass U.S. semiconductor export restrictions. The unit focuses on illicit procurement of restricted high-end Nvidia AI chips and intelligence gathering on key chip executives to counter Western technological blockades.

items.title: Tesla rolls out FSD v15, featuring a photorealistic rendering of car surroundings; Elon Musk says it is real-time AI video generation without using game engines (Mike Pearl/Gizmodo)
items.content_text: Tesla has rolled out FSD v15 to select vehicles this Saturday, featuring a visualization system that abandons game engine rendering in favor of real-time AI video generation. This transition represents a shift in Tesla's perception architecture from traditional rule-based rendering to end-to-end generative AI synthesis for real-time environment representation.

items.title: A joint statement by the Lean and Mathlib communities says "we have full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct" (Lean community blog)
items.content_text: Mathematician Levent Alpöge released a formal proof of the Riemann Hypothesis on November 20, 2026, consisting of 17 million lines of Lean code relying on the Mathlib library. The Lean and Mathlib communities have officially certified the proof's correctness after comprehensive verification of its logic and codebase.

items.title: Tech suppliers raise AI server prices up to 45% months after deals are signed
items.content_text: Global data center equipment suppliers are significantly increasing prices for previously contracted AI servers, with hikes reaching up to 45%. This surge is driven by extreme supply-demand imbalances in AI infrastructure, forcing manufacturers to bypass existing contract terms to pass on rising memory and component costs.

items.title: The Alice Huang Associate Accused of Funneling Nvidia Chips to China
items.content_text: Li Ming, a 52-year-old Chinese national based in Singapore, is accused of operating a smuggling network that funneled restricted Nvidia AI chips to China by utilizing front companies including Megaspeed. Li is currently out on bail, having played a central role in orchestrating the bypass of U.S. export controls.

items.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
items.content_text: Jakub Pachocki, Chief Scientist at OpenAI, advocates for establishing perplexity as the primary metric for comparing model developers' pretraining progress and safety standards. This move aims to standardize scientific measurement across the industry by increasing transparency in model performance.

items.title: The UN fails to agree on rules regulating ‘killer robots’
items.content_text: UN diplomats failed to establish a legally binding framework for lethal autonomous weapons systems at the Geneva meeting, settling only on a two-year window to discuss potential regulatory options. Led by Russia, Israel, and the United States, significant resistance has stalled progress on defining enforceable compliance standards.

items.title: Alice Huang’s links to the chip underworld
items.content_text: Former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang is accused of orchestrating a complex shell company network to illicitly transfer advanced Nvidia AI chips to China. The network engaged cloud providers, gambling entities, and Cambodian organizations, utilizing infrastructure linked to former Nvidia partner Inspur to bypass US export controls.

items.title: Amazon closes in on $7.5bn deal to buy AI start-up Decart
items.content_text: Amazon is in advanced negotiations to acquire AI startup Decart for approximately $7.5 billion. Decart's core software optimizes AI model efficiency to mitigate hardware bottlenecks, and the firm has already deeply integrated its stack with Amazon's proprietary Trainium3 AI chips.

items.title: Nvidia researchers argue huge AI context windows are a dead end
items.content_text: Nvidia researchers demonstrated that blindly scaling context windows to million-token levels is not the optimal path for LLM efficiency. Their findings indicate that combining periodic summarization with targeted information retrieval achieves comparable performance while significantly reducing computational costs and inference latency.

items.title: Silicon Valley's growing obsession with AI doomsday is turning parts of the tech industry toward cult-like devotion
items.content_text: Maple, founded in 2011 by Soryu Forall, is infiltrating Silicon Valley's AI engineering and data center management workforce through a narrative of AI apocalyptic salvation. Former members report that the organization imposes strict behavioral surveillance to harvest data for training an AI deity modeled after Forall's consciousness, currently generating up to $1 million in annual revenue.
